# This test verifies that MMA correctly filters out high disk utilization stores
# as rebalance targets, even when MMA has load-based motivation to use them.
#
# Key insight: We create a scenario where MMA WANTS to move replicas to s4/s5
# due to CPU load imbalance, but s4/s5 have high disk utilization (93%) which
# gives them ReplicaDispositionRefusing. This should prevent MMA from sending
# replicas there despite the load imbalance.
#
# Setup:
# - 5-node cluster, 10GiB stores
# - All replicas start on s1, s2, s3 with s1 as leaseholder (high CPU load on s1)
# - s4 and s5 start empty (no replicas) but have 93% disk utilization
# - CPU-heavy workload causes s1 to be overloaded
#
# Expected behavior:
# - MMA wants to balance CPU by moving replicas/leases away from s1
# - s4/s5 appear attractive (no load) but have disposition = Refusing
# - MMA should NOT move replicas to s4/s5 despite the load imbalance
# - Replicas should only move between s1, s2, s3 (all have OK disposition)
gen_cluster nodes=5 store_byte_capacity_gib=10
----

setting split_queue_enabled=false
----

setting replicate_queue_enabled=false
----

# All 20 ranges start on s1, s2, s3 with s1 as leaseholder.
# s4 and s5 have no replicas initially.
gen_ranges ranges=20 repl_factor=3 placement_type=replica_placement
{s1:*,s2,s3}:20
----
{s1:*,s2,s3}:20

# Store 4: 93% disk utilization (above 92.5% refuse threshold)
# Should refuse new replicas despite having no load
set_capacity store=4 capacity=10737418240 available=752414918
----

# Store 5: 93% disk utilization (above 92.5% refuse threshold)
# Should refuse new replicas despite having no load
set_capacity store=5 capacity=10737418240 available=752414918
----

# CPU-heavy workload: s1 (leaseholder) gets high CPU load.
# This creates motivation for MMA to move leases/replicas to balance CPU.
# Without disk utilization filtering, MMA would want to use s4/s5 (no load).
gen_load rate=5000 rw_ratio=1.0 min_block=1 max_block=1 cpu_per_access=10000
----
0.05 vcpus

# s4 and s5 should have 0 replicas despite MMA's desire to balance load there.
# This proves the disk utilization-based ReplicaDispositionRefusing works.
assertion type=stat stat=replicas stores=(4) exact_bound=0 ticks=6
----

assertion type=stat stat=replicas stores=(5) exact_bound=0 ticks=6
----

# Verify MMA does NOT move replicas to s4/s5 despite load imbalance.
# Even though s4/s5 have zero load and would help balance CPU,
# their high disk utilization (93%) means disposition = Refusing.
# Results should show s4=0 and s5=0 replicas throughout.
eval duration=6m seed=42 metrics=(disk_fraction_used,replicas,leases,cpu) cfgs=(mma-only)
----
